fact: The territorial administration ministry (MATGLAC) officially launched the re-reading of law 2009-010 on the organisation of civil status on 21 August 2026, with OIF technical and financial support and UNECA technical input; its director of territorial administration said the reform must take in the digitisation of civil status and the interoperability of systems, across the 117 communes created since the law.

MATGLAC opened a three-day technical workshop on 8 September 2026 for the support unit re-reading the 2009 civil status law, with UNECA expertise; a diagnosis of the law's application is to precede a new or amending law.

Togo First reports that the Ministry of Territorial Administration began a review of the 2009 civil registration law at a scoping meeting in Lomé 'last week' (the week of 17-21 August 2026), to reflect decentralisation, the digitalisation of procedures and interoperability between administrative systems, with reform proposals expected before the end of 2026.

fact: WHO's Togo office reports that in 2024 it supported a national diagnostic of the birth and death registration system, which produced a national roadmap for the digitalisation of CRVS and a multisectoral task force to harmonise practice.

Law 2009-010 (art. 2) places civil registration under the joint supervision of the minister for territorial administration and the minister for justice, who organise, run and control it; declarations are received in the communes by mayors or their delegates (art. 5), and communes buy the registers on the ministry's single model (art. 9).
